detection.scope: Image-level presence of local diffusion editing, evaluated separately from the spatial/model-aware tasks.
detection.decision_rule: p7: classify an image as edited when its predicted non-background mask area exceeds 1% of total image area.
detection.evaluation: Table5 p7 reports binary classification Acc and mAP; Table6 p7 reports cross-generator binary classification. Segmentation models are adapted by mask-area thresholding, not by a generator-ID image classifier.
detection.limits: The paper does not detail a continuous score used to compute mAP or a separate pixel probability cutoff. It does not establish whole-image model-ID classification.

localization.scope: Learned per-pixel edited-region predictions assessed against editing-mask ground truth.
localization.prediction: Binary foreground/background segmentation by trained FCN-8s, SegFormer-B2 and DeepLabv3+ baselines.
localization.ground_truth: Object masks from Grounded-SAM define the known inpainting regions in the editing pipeline; they are evaluation targets, separate from each baseline’s predicted masks. These are not merely baseline explanation or attention maps.
localization.evaluation: Main Table2 p5 binary pixel accuracy, foreground mIoU and boundary-F1; Table3 p5 distortion stress tests; Table4 p7 binary cross-generator segmentation.
localization.limits: Masks are constructed automatically, with acknowledged mask errors and quality filtering; no independent manual pixel-perfect validation is reported.

source_attribution.scope: Closed-set editing-model identity assigned per edited pixel/region as model-aware semantic segmentation.
source_attribution.prediction: A spatial class map over background and eight editing-model classes. Model identity is part of the predicted mask, rather than a domain label applied only when tabulating results.
source_attribution.main_evaluation_proof: Table2 explicitly evaluates semantic segmentation as localization plus attribution to specific diffusion models; Figure5 compares predicted versus true values for the nine named classes. Thus the result exceeds an annotation-schema or dataset-capability claim.
source_attribution.main_metrics: Class-aware semantic mIoU, semantic boundary-F1 and pixel accuracy in Table2; class-specific normalized confusion entries in Figure5.
source_attribution.not_required: A separate whole-image generator classifier is not needed for this demonstrated regional attribution task.
source_attribution.not_established: Global source-model identification for a mixed-source image, attribution of the original base-image generator, complete editing history, and open-set identification of unseen editing models are not established.

labels_outputs_and_training.numeric_encoding_boundary: The user-supplied dataset schema describes background0 and model IDs1–8. The full PDF displays background plus eight named predicted/true classes, but does not itself spell out a numeric ID-to-model mapping. Figure5’s plotting order must not be assumed to equal dataset integer encoding. Any card-sourced 0..8 mapping should have separate provenance.
labels_outputs_and_training.model_identity_vs_content: Unlike the earlier T056/T345 cases, the semantic prediction classes here are actual named editing models, not object content categories or generator names used only as evaluation domains.
labels_outputs_and_training.architectures: Section4.1 pp4–5: FCN-8s and DeepLabv3+ with ResNet50, plus SegFormer-B2. Both binary and model-aware semantic segmentation are explicitly trained/evaluated.
labels_outputs_and_training.output_detail_boundary: The paper establishes the categorical output spaces through task definitions and confusion matrices, but does not specify final layer channel dimensions, activation details or implementation-level mask decoding. Nine semantic classes are supported; precise tensor shape is not independently reported.
labels_outputs_and_training.losses_and_equations: No explicit numbered task-loss equations or novel classification/localization objective are given. The benchmark uses default hyperparameters from existing implementations; a particular cross-entropy implementation must not be inferred as a paper-specified detail.
labels_outputs_and_training.training_and_validation: 8:2 train/validation split, all results on validation; 512x512 baseline training; 5,000 additional unedited real COCO training images to suppress segmentation false positives; approximate training times FCN/SegFormer/DeepLab 8/6/3h on a4090.
labels_outputs_and_training.classification_negative_training: p8: additionally30,000 real COCO images are used as negatives when training CNNSpot and UniversalFakeDet classification baselines.
labels_outputs_and_training.split_limits: Exact per-task validation counts and the separation of related editing sequences/base images are not specified. The distribution/split of negative real evaluation samples is not fully detailed.

construction_and_multi_turn_semantics.construction: Qwen2.5-VL identifies object categories; Grounded-SAM supplies object masks. Candidate masks with pairwise IoU>70% are removed as redundant. One to three masks are randomly selected. For each selected region, a VLM generates an attribute/add/remove prompt and a randomly selected one of eight diffusion models performs inpainting.
construction_and_multi_turn_semantics.multi_turn: An edited image is paired with remaining masks for up to three sequential turns. p8 explicitly describes images with multiple interleaved edited regions from different generators. Thus more than one model identity can occur in a single image.
construction_and_multi_turn_semantics.model_choice_limit: Random selection from eight models does not demonstrate that every turn in every image uses a distinct model or sampling without replacement.
construction_and_multi_turn_semantics.base_images: About half are real COCO bases and half generated from COCO-derived prompts. Figure3 reports47.9% real-base and52.1% AI-base; edit-turn distribution10.0% one,38.7% two and51.3% three.
construction_and_multi_turn_semantics.background_scope: The semantic background means not locally edited by the benchmark operation; it is not a guarantee of camera-origin authenticity, since AI-generated bases are included. The task attributes local inpainting operations rather than all original-image synthesis.
construction_and_multi_turn_semantics.overlap_finding: The paper filters highly overlapping duplicate masks at IoU>70%, but that does not rule out partial overlap. No explicit rule for resolving labels in overlapping sequential edits, overwriting/last-writer ownership, recovering earlier covered edits, or separately evaluating overwritten regions appears in the17-page PDF.
construction_and_multi_turn_semantics.evaluation_boundary: Figure5 shows a mutually exclusive categorical prediction map, with one named class per evaluated pixel. This supports final visible-region model-aware segmentation as evaluated, while it does not establish reconstruction of all historical sources on overwritten pixels. A last-write annotation rule must remain unverified unless independently sourced from permitted dataset documentation.
construction_and_multi_turn_semantics.quality_limit: A VLM quality score<3 discards approximately50% of generated candidates; the paper acknowledges quality scoring may use the whole image and erroneously filter acceptable edits. Automatic masks may be imperfect.

segmentation: mIoU, called mask Intersection-over-Union in Section4.1; semantic class-aware evaluation, exact averaging formula not given
metric_definition.metric_limit: Boundary-F1 is a spatial boundary measure, not macro-F1 over model identities. Confusion-matrix diagonal entries are not per-model IoU. Results below are reported by the paper, not independently rerun.

Table2_p5_baseline_tasks.interpretation: The semantic mIoUs are measured on editing-model-specific predicted classes, distinct from the stronger binary foreground localization mIoUs. This is a main-paper quantitative attribution result.

Figure5_p7_semantic_confusions.axes: True Label versus Predicted Label for BG plus8 named editing-model classes.
Figure5_p7_semantic_confusions.interpretation: These are displayed normalized class-confusion diagonal values, not per-model IoUs or image-level model-ID accuracy. SegFormerFlux→SD2 confusion is0.12; DeepLab has lower correct Kolors/SDXL proportions0.72/0.76. The named predicted-class axes directly demonstrate evaluated identity prediction.

Table3_p5_transformations.interpretation: Semantic attribution performance is fragile under distortions, particularly JPEG. Weak robustness does not erase the existence of the evaluated task.

Table4_p7_binary_cross_generator_segment.training: Six known editing models; evaluate edits from two unseen models, using binary segmentation. Baseline uses all8 models.
Table4_p7_binary_cross_generator_segment.boundary: This experiment supports transferable binary localization, not identification of unknown model classes. Do not promote these generator-domain columns to additional attribution evidence.

Table5_p7_binary_image_classification.decision: Predict edited when non-background mask fraction>0.01.
Table5_p7_binary_image_classification.interpretation: An independently reported image-level edited/unedited evaluation, not generator-ID classification.

Table6_p7_binary_classification_cross_ge.boundary: Six-train/two-held-out generator split measures edited-image detection transfer only.
